prov.text: Credit loss expense. The Company recorded a credit loss expense of $1.1 million and a $0.76 million expense for the three months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, respectively. The increase primarily reflects continued growth in the loan portfolio and management’s evaluation of the qualitative and quantitative factors used to estimate expected credit losses. Expected credit losses are charged to earnings to maintain the allowance for credit losses at a level deemed appropriate by management to absorb losses expected. Management’s periodic evaluation of the adequacy of the allowance for credit losses is based upon historical experience, the volume and composition of the loan portfolio, adverse situations that may affect the borrower’s ability to repay, estimated value of the underlying collateral, general economic conditions, particularly within the Company’s market areas, and other factors affecting the estimated collectability of loans. The allowance for credit losses totaled $12.1 million, or 0.89% of total loans outstanding, at September 30, 2026, compared to $10.3 million, or 1.07% of total loans outstanding, at December 31, 2025. Net charge-offs during the three months ended September 30, 2026 totaled $11,000 and were limited to the consumer loan portfolio.

nonint.text: Noninterest expenses . Total noninterest expenses increased to $9 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $6.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, primarily due to employee compensation and benefits, data processing fees, and other expenses.

nonop.text: The following table sets forth, for the periods indicated, information regarding (i) the total dollar amount of interest and dividend income of the Company from interest-earning assets and the resultant average yields; (ii) the total dollar amount of interest expense on interest-bearing liabilities and the resultant average cost; (iii) net interest income; (iv) interest-rate spread; (v) net interest margin; and (vi) the ratio of average interest-earning assets to average interest-bearing liabilities.

net.text: Net income . Net income for the three months ended September 30, 2026, was $7.2 million or $0.30 per basic and per diluted earnings per share, compared to net income of $4.3 million or $0.37 per basic earnings per share and $0.18 per diluted earnings per share for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The Company’s strong financial performance during the quarter was primarily driven by growth in net interest income and noninterest income, reflecting continued execution of its relationship-based banking strategy.

Net interest income.text: The following table sets forth, for the periods indicated, information regarding (i) the total dollar amount of interest and dividend income of the Company from interest-earning assets and the resultant average yields; (ii) the total dollar amount of interest expense on interest-bearing liabilities and the resultant average cost; (iii) net interest income; (iv) interest-rate spread; (v) net interest margin; and (vi) the ratio of average interest-earning assets to average interest-bearing liabilities.

Noninterest income.text: Noninterest income. Total noninterest income was $2.8 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $2.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was primarily due to $0.9 million of nonrecurring late fees collected on the payoff of a nonaccrual loan and higher wire transfer and ACH fees, partially offset by lower gains on the sale of government guaranteed SBA loans.
